newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods split with NYMEX, diffs close firmer.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods split with NYMEX, diffs close firmer.

text.p: U.S. spot refinery products ended mixed Monday, led by choppy trade on the NYMEX floor and modest gains in gasoline differentials.

NYMEX heating oil futures settled slightly weaker Monday, while December gasoline futures ended slightly higher on calendar spread trading, with little impact felt from news that the U.N.-Iraq oil-for-food deal could be nearing implementation.
Gasoline trade held center ring in the market with both U.S. Gulf (USG) and New York Harbor (NYH) barrels attracting steady buying interest, according to traders.
Overall market interest appeared fairly thin, with some players out of the market ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.
"Those that needed barrels probably already got it done," one trader said.

NYH conventional prompt M5 unleaded gasoline diffs firmed to about 2.50 cents over the NYMEX, up about 0.50 cents from Friday's levels, while prompt reformulated A5 87-octane gasoline jumped to about 3.50 cents, according to traders.
USG prompt conventional M4 gasoline also strengthened, market players said, moving to 1.50 cents under the screen.
Gulf activity could pick up Tuesday, which is the scheduling deadline for A4 reformulated gasoline for the 33rd cycle on the Colonial Pipeline, one trader said.
Heating oil activity remained lackluster, though players said a few small parcels changed hands.
Few concerns emerged regarding the colder temperatures expected to hit the Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market. "There's plenty of barrels available," one trader said.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1620
